title: Cost invariance under derandomization
statement: Let $p$ be a one-way public-coin protocol over a shared randomness type $\Omega$, with input types $X$, $Y$ and output type $\alpha$, and let $\omega \in \Omega$ be a fixed coin outcome. Then the deterministic one-way protocol obtained from $p$ by substituting $\omega$ for the public randomness has the same communication cost as $p$; that is, both have cost $\lceil \log_2 |M| \rceil$ bits, where $M$ is the shared message codebook.
hypotheses_covered: public-coin protocol p over randomness type Omega with inputs X, Y and output alpha
fixed coin outcome omega in Omega
replaced:
For any public-coin protocol $p$ and coin outcome $\omega$,
\[
  (p.\mathrm{toDeterministic}(\omega)).\mathrm{cost} \;=\; p.\mathrm{cost}.
\]
Fixing the randomness does not change the communication cost of the protocol.
